sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Manufacturing expansion with contestable customer relationships, not an established compounder. Fresh IPO capital and operating margin improvement are real, but acquisition scope, accounting restatements and cash-flow discrepancies prevent a favorable investment conclusion. The completed conditional model gives bear/base/bull exit prices of ₹17.65/238.18/641.08 against the dated ₹288.95 quote, with annualized returns −46.67%/−4.25%/+19.63%. These are assumptions, not target-price assurances. G2 remains Hold — unresolved. [S1][S2][S95]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026; BSE SME 544670, ISIN INE1IJQ01026. Listing 31 December 2025, current 2.14044 crore shares and 600-share lot. FY26 consolidated Indian GAAP/AS includes wholly owned Mundada Polymers; FY25 annual comparison is standalone, while prospectus restatements differ. Units: ₹ crore. Quote is the secondary 19 October close, not live. Audited 31 March opening balances are a pro-forma model reference; full FY27 includes months before entry and is not an observed October balance. Exit 31 March 2031,15% nominal shareholder hurdle,₹5 lakh reference position. Historical extraction is Medium confidence, cash reconciliation/organic growth Low, conditional valuation Medium, overall Low. [S1][S2][S91][S95]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 4, DUR 5, CAP 5, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 5 have Medium-confidence evidence. REV and CASH remain NS because scope and financial reconciliation are missing, not because growth or cash weakness was automatically assigned a neutral score. R 1, D 2, P 1 and conditional L 7 reflect the computed reference case and liquidity constraints. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS with original-weight coverage and bounds. No persistent-capital/cash override is inferred from an immature cohort or an unresolved number. G2 excludes favorable classification. Detailed arithmetic and counterevidence accompany the factors.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company sells PET preforms and caps/closures to beverage, FMCG, dairy and other users. Revenue is product/service sales, not order book or customer logos. Management describes per-unit negotiated pricing with resin pass-through, so revenue growth can include resin price and mix rather than volume. Four rigid plants and a new flexible-packaging subsidiary share an asset-intensive supply chain. The prospectus records 822 H1 FY26 customers and 164 repeat customers over four years; this supports a franchise but is not an audited retention rate. The subsidiary was incorporated 5 February 2026 to acquire a promoter-relative-owned proprietorship; its short reported period cannot be annualized into proven organic growth. [S1][S2][S7][S9][S11][S12]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: MOAT 4: molding quality, customer qualification and delivery relationships can reduce switching, but machinery and certifications are purchasable and geographical freight costs encourage regional competitors. FY25 Maharashtra exposure 75.58%, top 10 customers 40%, and absence of major-supplier long-term contracts constrain bargaining power. CRISIL describes successful resin pass-through alongside limited pricing flexibility and fragmented competition, not contradictory proof of a durable premium. Repeat business is the positive counterweight. Cool Caps is a direct caps/preform/trading comparator: FY26 consolidated revenue₹530.8871 crore, but strict EBITDA=(PBT 11.1655+finance 12.6472+DA 8.3110−other 26.0374)=₹6.0863 crore, only 1.15%; PAT depends heavily on other income. Its sales growth is not a suitable earnings multiple for Bai. Other peer and mix differences are documented rather than applying a sector-average P/E. [S2][S13][S15] Technopack Polymers is a smaller direct preform/closure peer: FY26 sales₹8.3741 crore versus₹17.2815 crore prior year, strict EBITDA₹2.9062 crore or34.7%, yet revenue halved. Manjushree’s FY25 standalone sales₹2,569.8263 crore and strict EBITDA₹397.1975 crore or15.46% represent a much larger, diversified comparator; reported PAT includes₹176.9015 crore exceptional gain, principally CCD conversion. These three peers show why size, trading mix, inventory movements and exceptional income matter more than sector labels. No live peer P/E is imported. [S16][S17]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Restated standalone FY23/24/25 revenue₹272.8791/294.8145/325.9292 crore gives a two-year CAGR 9.29%, not a three-year CAGR. Annual additions₹21.9354/31.1147 crore. H1 FY26 restated revenue₹162.1105 crore is seasonal half-year data, not an annual forecast. FY26 annual standalone₹354.1469 crore grows 8.84% versus annual FY25₹325.3674 crore; consolidated₹364.689 crore adds₹10.5421 crore versus parent scope, not independently measured organic growth. March 2025 business transfer, FY26 subsidiary takeover and differing restatements prevent a preferred three/five-year comparable organic series. The May presentation’s FY23₹229 crore history and approximate rigid/flexible₹351/14 crore mix do not reconcile to the restated series. REV remains NS; no artificial acquisition haircut or best-period selection. [S1][S2][S9]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: DUR 5: utilized PET/closure capacity and recurring packaging demand give an accessible existing market, while recycled PET, solar and flexible films introduce commissioning, regulation and customer-qualification constraints. Management reports PET 22,600 tonnes at about 90% utilization, closures about 500 crore units at 84%, and flexible 8,460 tonnes at about 90%; none supplies unlimited spare capacity. The base therefore funds 12% revenue growth with maintenance₹12 crore annually plus incremental sales/2 asset investment, and a first-year₹7.2665 crore contractual commitment. Opening capital advances₹10.7248 crore reduce cash paid once, not physical capacity needs. CAP 5: a restated FY23–25 financing-capital proxy including CWIP suggests about 14.33% incremental post-tax operating return against an assumed 12–16% nominal cost-of-capital range, but the business transfer distorts attribution. FY25 annual-to-FY26 total funding-capital expansion is much faster than strict NOPAT, around 4.8% incremental proxy, with new assets immature. This is mixed cohort evidence, not a proven project IRR or persistent destruction. [S1][S2][S8][S9]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: GOV 5 and EXEC 5 balance operating delivery against unresolved stewardship details. September 15 voting results confirm the Aquasure material RPT resolution passed, with promoters abstaining and 171,000 public noninstitutional votes supporting it; only 0.80% of total shares voted on that item. Approval does not establish independent pricing or collectability. FY26 transactions₹31.26 crore and FY27 cap₹100 crore remain material. The February loan agreement permits up to₹10 crore to the wholly owned subsidiary at 7.5% for up to five years, to acquire a promoter-relative-owned proprietorship; the incorporation disclosures do not supply the completed consideration/valuation bridge. Consolidated analysis eliminates the parent/subsidiary loan, not the economic cost of the acquired business. IPO monitoring reports no object deviation and full deployment:₹64 crore debt,₹9.85 crore machinery,₹12.94 crore solar,₹7.14 crore GCP and₹11.24 crore expenses;₹0.36 crore expense saving moved to GCP. No residual IPO cash is invented. These completed funding milestones support execution, while RPET claims remain unverified future capability. Historical rating noncooperation was resolved in March 2025; June 2026 rating is BBB+/Stable, not a current default or an equity endorsement. [S1][S6][S7][S8][S11][S12][S13][S14]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 strict EBITDA₹48.7804 crore excludes₹10.0862 crore other income and₹3.4426 crore prior-period credit; EBIT₹30.3547 crore, reported PAT₹26.9768 crore. Removing the credit at an assumed 25% marginal tax gives₹24.39485 crore normalized PAT, not an issuer-restated amount. Other income includes subsidy₹5.04 crore and commission₹2.4428 crore; future reference EBITDA does not capitalize them. Current-share EPS is₹12.60 reported/₹11.40 conditionally normalized versus₹15.69 historical weighted EPS; IPO dilution means headline PAT growth is not per-share growth. Restated FY23–25 CFO totals₹46.0992 crore/PAT₹31.9304 crore=1.444 x, but FY25 annual CFO −₹9.926 crore contradicts prospectus+₹11.7335 crore. Interest sign and scope differences do not fully reconcile it. FY26 CFO₹28.0352 crore minus PPE cash₹65.8787 crore=−₹37.8435 crore, or−₹43.5753 crore with capital advances. Cash/bank balance is₹2.5205 crore, not the MD&A-mislabeled receivable figure₹38.9371 crore; true cash equivalents₹0.5132 crore. Receivables 1–2 years₹1.8966 crore and provision₹0.0697 crore require collection monitoring. Gratuity obligation₹0.2114 crore has no positive plan assets in the closing summary; current₹0.0098 crore settles within provisions and noncurrent₹0.2016 crore remains a terminal claim. The anomalous negative-plan-asset table is not treated as usable cash. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At the 19 October secondary₹288.95 close,2.14044 crore shares imply₹618.4801 crore equity capitalization. Starting debt₹65.7281 crore is netted only with cash equivalents₹0.5132 crore for immediate funding. Deposits₹10.5753 crore are not proven restricted: the reference retains their recoverable value at exit, and a separate immediate-availability case tests funding. Opening operating WC₹60.2347 crore excludes capital advances, tax/CSR earmarks, subsidies and separately retained deposits/interest, while trade payables and full other current liabilities remain inside WC. Net current provisions₹4.0777 crore settle once after TDS₹0.0107 crore and CSRcash₹0.1404 crore offsets. Subsidy receivable₹13.3711 crore is recovered over two years in the base, not counted again in WC or terminal value; zero-recovery sensitivity is explicit. No future subsidy income is assumed in reference cases. Bear/base/bull revenue growth paths−10/0/3/3/3%,12% and 20%; EBITDA margins 9.5/13/15.5%; WC 23/18/16% of revenue; exitEBIT multiples 6/10/14. Debt costs 13/11/10% include half-year draw interest. Depreciation follows 12% of average modeled net assets, explicitly an estimate, and capex is linked to growth. Required new borrowing₹12.32/1.62/3.06 crore is conditional, not committed. Full annual cash, debt, physical-capex, impairment and retained-claim bridges, FCFF discount sensitivities and margin/multiple grid are attached. The conditional base return−4.25% is below 15%; no favorable entry conclusion survives G2. [S1][S2][S8][S13][S95] The conditional 15% hurdle entry value is₹127.95, with 12%/18% hurdle sensitivities₹143.91/114.11. Retained deposits earn no separately forecast interest in the reference, a conservative assumption rather than a claim that deposits earn nothing; the separate₹5.04 crore other-income case bounds recurring subsidy economics. Opening deferred tax₹2.4117 crore is also retained as a terminal claim because modeled book and tax depreciation are assumed equal; it is not paid immediately or counted twice in annual taxes. The₹0.0314 crore difference between the short-term-advance note and balance sheet remains in broad WC using the balance-sheet total, not silently corrected.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The bear combines lower demand/margin, WC absorption and₹8.9808 crore noncash inventory/receivable impairment. Recoverable opening WC is reduced by that amount, so replacement funding appears once throughΔWC; the impairment is added back in CFO, not paid again as cash. Half subsidy and half terminal nonoperating recovery are assumptions, not quoted recovery values. Bear exit₹17.65 implies about 93.9% capital loss, and borrowing is still required. No-new-debt base fails its funding constraint and has no valid shareholder-return output. Other sensitivities isolate deposit availability, subsidy delay/loss,11% margin,25% WC, no nonoperating recovery and contingent calls₹3.5882 crore. Parent guarantees for subsidiary facilities are not added again to consolidated debt. Permanent-loss pathways are unsuccessful reinvestment, uncollected receivables/subsidies and recapitalization, not an allegation of misconduct. [S1]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: The completed reverse model solves the revenue growth needed for the 15% hurdle and 5×/10× terminal share prices at unchanged base margin/valuation parameters. It scales physical capex and working capital with revenue, charges draw interest and reports cumulative new financing. These extreme solutions do not demonstrate demand, available sites, RPET approval or lending access. Reported revenue growth or a higher exit multiple alone cannot establish a multibagger; detailed solved growth, terminal revenue, capex and financing are in the linked reverse-expectations table. No promotional probability is assigned. At base 13% margin / 10× EBIT, the15% hurdle requires about46.07% revenue CAGR, terminal sales₹2424.77 crore and conditional new borrowing₹905.18 crore. The 5×/10× solutions require about85.38%/115.20% growth and terminal sales₹7983.40/₹16832.65 crore. These implausibly large financing/capacity requirements are disconfirming constraints, not forecasts.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Before changing G2, obtain a signed restated-versus-annual FY25 CFO bridge and the nature/tax treatment of the₹3.4426 crore FY26 prior-period credit. Track subsidy collections versus₹13.3711 crore, deposits and restrictions versus₹10.5753 crore, net current provisions versus₹4.0777 crore modeled settlement, aged receivables and remaining capital advances. Require the completed related-party takeover consideration, acquired balances and independent valuation, not just WOS incorporation. Compare subsequent capacity output and new customer revenue with capex; verify actual RPET approvals rather than an ambiguous rating reference to another acronym. Margin below 11%, WC above 25% or unavailable incremental financing triggers the modeled stress review, not an automatic trading instruction. Update quote, corporate actions, lot and executable depth for any actual position. [S1][S6][S7][S13]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved / insufficient reliable evidence for a favorable investment conclusion. Manufacturing growth optionality exists, but current price embeds more than the conditional base earns, and unresolved cash/scope issues prevent aggregate ranking. Completion of this research is not clearance of the company. Reconsider only after reconciliations and financing evidence, with updated model and dated executable liquidity; no portfolio allocation is inferred.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual report and prospectus were inspected across statements, notes, restatements, related parties and capital history, then supplemented with AGM voting, loan/incorporation filings, IPO monitoring and rating rationales. Issuer index now exposes approval evidence absent from the earlier review. No correction resolving FY25 CFO was located. The rating narrative changes consolidation scope but its entity annexure remains inconsistent, and its same-year growth/NFPL references are not imported as verified company facts. AOC1 does not provide a usable complete subsidiary financial bridge in the inspected report. Secondary OHLCV supplies the dated quote and conditional capacity, not actual BSE traded value or clearance. Sources distinguish verified disclosures, management claims, calculations and assumptions; framework weights are research-policy choices, not validated return predictors. [S1][S2][S6][S8][S13][S95]
